title: Normalize conversational chat into supported machine-actionable commands
goal: Normalize common conversational Vietnamese and English lead-ins into the existing strict workspace command grammar so the Agent can identify actionable intent without treating arbitrary chat as executable instructions.
context: A successful workspace file-write report shows the production command path can execute a supported request. The current command normalizer recognizes only a narrow set of polite lead-ins, so natural user phrasing may fail to reach the same deterministic parser. Normalization must remain separate from capability authorization and execution verification.
forbidden_changes: Do not weaken workspace-only path restrictions, schema validation, policy or approval checks, protected-path checks, file size limits, cancellation, or read-back verification.
Do not convert arbitrary free-form chat into an executable command unless it matches the supported grammar.
Do not treat model-generated prose or a write response as proof of verified execution.
Do not modify release workflows or claim physical-device acceptance without testing a real iPhone.
acceptance_criteria: Common English conversational lead-ins and supported Vietnamese polite lead-ins normalize to the existing command grammar deterministically.
Preflight and Skill input extraction agree on the supported lead-ins.
Incomplete, ambiguous, and unsafe file requests continue to ask for clarification or fail closed without invoking a write module.
Regression tests cover normalization and preflight acceptance for the new variants.
Existing workspace path policy and read-back verification behavior remain unchanged.
All required CI checks pass on the proposed commit; physical-device acceptance remains separate under Issue #347.
verification: Inspect Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA workflow results.
Record physical iPhone verification separately on Issue #347.
recovery: If a normalized phrase is ambiguous or unsupported by the strict file parser, remove that lead-in and return a clarification rather than widening the executable grammar.
